title: Month-2 Retention Rate Calculation
description:
Calculate the retention rate: what percentage of users who were active in January 2026 also returned in February 2026?

**Table: user_sessions** — `user_id`, `session_month`

Output columns: `month1_users`, `month2_retained`, `retention_rate_pct`.
solution_sql: WITH month1_users AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM user_sessions WHERE session_month = '2026-01'), month2_users AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM user_sessions WHERE session_month = '2026-02') SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT m1.user_id) AS month1_users, COUNT(DISTINCT m2.user_id) AS month2_retained, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT m2.user_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT m1.user_id), 2) AS retention_rate_pct FROM month1_users m1 LEFT JOIN month2_users m2 ON m1.user_id = m2.user_id

test_cases.description: 5 users active in Jan; users 1,2,3 also active in Feb; retention = 3/5 = 60.00% — 1 row

hints: Use two CTEs to isolate Jan users and Feb users separately, then LEFT JOIN on user_id and count non-NULL matches.
User 6 was active in Feb but not Jan — they do not affect the denominator since we start from the Jan cohort.
explanation: month1_users CTE finds 5 distinct users active in Jan. month2_users finds 4 in Feb (users 1,2,3,6). LEFT JOIN m1 ON m2.user_id keeps all 5 Jan users and matches those who returned. Users 1,2,3 match (retained=3). Users 4 and 5 did not return. User 6 is irrelevant — they weren't in Jan. Retention = 3/5 = 60.00%.
